notes: Retrieval labels for the sample SOC 2 report. 'evidence' lists short verbatim phrases from the report; a retrieved chunk counts as evidence if it contains any of them (case- and quote-insensitive). Questions are worded the way questionnaires ask, not copied from the report. 'answerable: false' questions cover topics the report never mentions. The five spec sample questions also carry a 'target' answer and automatic checks: every 'must_mention' group needs at least one of its phrases in the answer, and no 'must_not_mention' phrase may appear (case-insensitive).

questions.question: Do you have formally defined criteria for notifying a client during an incident that might impact the security of their data or systems? What are your SLAs for notification?
evidence: inform all necessary parties of the incident without undue delay
questions.target: No formal client-notification criteria or notification SLA are stated. The incident management procedures (5.12, p.21) say Nave will inform all necessary parties of an incident without undue delay, and a Breach Notification Policy exists (5.7, p.20).

questions.question: Is personal information transmitted, processed, stored, or disclosed to or retained by third parties? If yes, describe.
evidence: Agreements with vendors and service providers involved in accessing
questions.target: Yes: customer data is hosted with GCP, a subservice organization, and the report lists other third parties (Drata, Trello, Snyk, ...). Agreements with vendors that access, process or store information are reviewed before execution (p.40).

questions.question: Which cloud providers do you rely on?
evidence: uses a subservice organization for cloud hosting services
questions.target: GCP (Google Cloud Platform) is the cloud hosting provider (p.17; a subservice organization for cloud hosting, p.9).

questions.question: Please specify the primary data center location/region of the underlying cloud infrastructure used to host the service(s), as well as the backup location(s).
evidence: multiple availability zones to replicate production data
questions.target: No primary or backup region is named. Production data is hosted on GCP and replicated across multiple availability zones (p.81; multi-availability zone deployment, p.22); backups run at least daily.

questions.question:
Which of the following, if any, are performed as part of your monitoring process for the service?
- Application Performance Monitoring (APM)
- End User Monitoring (EUM)
- Digital Experience Monitoring (DEM)
questions.target: None of APM, EUM or DEM is named. The report describes GCP-provided monitoring of network and systems: CPU and memory alerts, application error counts, disk space, SSL certificate expiry and service uptime checks (5.11, p.21).
